passage:
Shreya: heads up. Lata in accounts told me Nisha is saying you got the transfer because of your uncle
Manjula: what? my uncle doesn't even work here
Manjula: everyone has probably heard it. I feel so exposed 😔
Shreya: want me to say something to Nisha?
Manjula: no. I'll ask her directly tomorrow over tea
Shreya: what will you say
Manjula: "I heard a story about my transfer. Can we talk about what you heard?" no accusing
Manjula: and I'm not going to spread anything about her either
Shreya: good. people work out who's honest over time
Manjula: I'll keep doing my work. tell you how the tea goes

qa.q: Who told Shreya about the rumour?

qa.a: Manjula thinks everyone may already have heard the rumour about the transfer.

qa.q: How does Manjula plan to respond?
qa.a: Ask Nisha directly and calmly over tea, without accusing her and without spreading anything back.

qa.q: How might Nisha see the tea conversation?
qa.a: Nisha may be caught off guard, but a calm question gives her room to explain instead of starting a fight.

grounding: A colleague spreads a rumour; the protagonist stays calm, asks the colleague directly and refuses to fight back with gossip.

passage: "You know what the worst part was? Not the rumour itself. It was walking into the pantry and everyone going quiet. Vishal had been telling people I got the Pune posting because I'm friendly with the regional head's nephew. I'm Arnab, I'd been on that team four years, and suddenly I felt like I was standing there in my vest. My first thought was to dig up something about Vishal. I actually had a story. I didn't use it. Next day I asked him, just the two of us, 'Did you say this?' He mumbled something about joking. I said, 'It isn't a joke to me. Please stop.' Then I just kept doing my work properly, on time, in the open. Three months on, nobody mentions it. People watched what I did, not what he said."

qa.q: What had Vishal been telling people?
qa.a: That Arnab got the Pune posting because of being friendly with the regional head's nephew.

qa.q: How did Arnab feel walking into the pantry?
qa.a: Arnab felt exposed and humiliated, as if standing there in a vest, when everyone went quiet.

qa.q: Why was it wise for Arnab not to use the story about Vishal?
qa.a: Fighting back with another rumour would have made Arnab a gossip too; asking directly and working openly let a steady pattern speak instead.

qa.q: How might Vishal see the private question?
qa.a: Vishal likely felt caught and embarrassed, which is why he mumbled about joking; a calm question made the rumour harder to keep going.

grounding: The protagonist learns a colleague is spreading rumours, feels exposed, asks directly, refuses to retaliate, and lets consistent conduct restore the reputation.

passage:
Tuesday: At the lab where Rehana ran samples, a trainee whispered that Uma had told everyone Rehana "faked the calibration log". Rehana's cheeks went hot. She spent the whole evening rereading old logs, stomach tight.
Thursday: She asked Uma to step into the storeroom. "I heard you said I faked the log. Did you?"
Uma looked at the shelves. "I only said it looked odd."
"Then next time, ask me. Here's the log, signed and time-stamped." Rehana kept her voice level, though her hands were cold.
Five weeks later: Uma was the one who asked Rehana to double-check a tricky run. Nobody talked about the log anymore. Rehana had simply kept signing, dating and filing every entry the same careful way, and the new trainees now copied her method.

qa.q: Where did Rehana talk with Uma?
What was Rehana feeling on Tuesday evening?
qa.a: She felt exposed and anxious; her cheeks went hot and she reread old logs with a tight stomach.

qa.q: What kept Rehana's reputation safe over time?
qa.a: She asked Uma directly, showed the signed log calmly, then kept every entry careful and consistent, so her pattern of work outweighed the story.

qa.q: Why might Uma say it only "looked odd"?
qa.a: Uma was probably embarrassed at being confronted and tried to shrink the claim, so the calm question took the force out of the rumour.

grounding: A colleague spreads a rumour; the protagonist stays calm, asks directly, keeps her conduct clean, and lets a steady pattern rebuild her reputation.
